judgment.notes: At S003, M003 is instantiated with V=R, a=-R, b=R, f(s)=g(Phi(y,s)) and d(s)=∂j g(Phi(y,s)). Smoothness supplies the derivative at all real s, including endpoints; continuity supplies interval integrability. R>0 orders the endpoints, and both endpoint points lie outside C, for every y. At S004, M002 uses the two specified restricted Lebesgue measures and f=w. These measures are finite and s-finite, R has the required normed structures, and w is integrable on the product by continuity and boundedness on its compact support box. The coordinate measure identification justifies the integral on Q. Routine facts are justified in BG001–BG005. There are no E applications.

N002 at t0 gives the three integrable functions and their support in C. The smooth scalar product g has exactly the derivative displayed in F002. Its slice endpoint values vanish, so M003 gives F003. The displayed coordinate decomposition and M002 then give F004. Support restriction and linearity turn F004 into the sum of the two full-space integrals; dot symmetry and rearrangement give the minus sign and the requested factor order. There is no limit/interchange of derivatives and integrals to justify. Both arbitrary binders are then universally closed.
